title: Monthly teaching-hours progress
summary: See finished scheduled hours as a percentage of the published teaching hours for the month, with finished, total and remaining hours.
highlights: The indicator counts a class only after its scheduled end in Bologna time; an ongoing class remains in the hours left.
Course, search and My courses only filters apply to the full month. Hiding past classes or teacher names does not change the denominator.
View the selected month in Day, Week and Month, or the current month in List. The indicator refreshes while the page is open.
This measures scheduled time, not attendance, credits or learning completion. Empty, invalid or unavailable data never produces an assumed percentage.

title: Refreshed university directory and campus galleries
summary: Explore the four partners with redesigned university cards, clearer navigation and a full-screen campus-photo viewer.
highlights: University cards and partner-page layouts follow the Hub's navy, ivory and terracotta identity.
Open campus photographs in a gallery with previous/next controls, keyboard navigation and visible captions, credits and source links.
Track-aware routes, service search, practical links and university comparisons remain available without changing their underlying academic data.

title: A full-month calendar, Day view and optional teacher names
summary: Plan across Day, Week, Month and List with a redesigned timetable, tinted class dates and optional teacher names.
highlights: The complete Monday-to-Sunday month highlights lecture dates with counts and course-colour markers; choose a date to see its classes.
The new Day view keeps a focused daily agenda. The Show teacher checkbox is off by default and remembers the display choice on this device.
Updated navy, ivory and terracotta styling, course-workspace links and compact source labels work alongside existing filters, maps and calendar exports.
The official UniBo feed remains authoritative. A loading error is not shown as a confirmed empty timetable.

title: Explore the planned careers, events and gallery sections
summary: Browse the published structure previews for Beyond EU-HEM, Events and Gallery and see how each section is intended to develop.
highlights: Beyond EU-HEM outlines future career resources and the proposed approach to alumni insights.
Events explains the planned categories and reviewed publishing approach; Gallery explains its proposed public and member-only model.
These are structure previews, not live opportunity collections, event submission tools or a student-photo upload service.
Full collections, uploads and verified member access remain on the roadmap.

title: Redesigned course Schedule, Exam, Topics and Resources
summary: A consistent study workspace across all eight first-year courses makes class dates, assessments, topics and resources easier to browse.
highlights: Schedule presents class dates, module filters and map/calendar actions with clear source-error recovery.
Exam separates official dates and registration, existing assessment guidance and personal preparation; calendar-copy fallbacks remain labelled.
Topics offers searchable cards and preserved saved progress; Resources puts official platforms first with source labels, search and saved filters.
Existing readers, specialist course content, quizzes, bookmarks and direct links remain available. Official lectures stay on their original platforms.

title: A search-led Notes & Resources library
summary: Find courses and study materials faster through a compact search-led library, resource-first cards and a clearer personal study area.
highlights: Course cards emphasise available resources, with planning and exam details in expandable panels.
Search course names, official codes and lesson topics; larger result groups offer an accessible Show more action.
On phones, the course library comes before secondary panels. Glossary filtering and empty study-list guidance are clearer.
Existing progress, bookmarks, backup/restore and source-fallback distinctions are preserved.

title: Behind the Build: the effort behind the Hub
summary: Explore the project owner's 60-hour personal-effort estimate, its illustrative workstreams and the roles of human decisions and AI assistance.
highlights: Six expandable workstreams, an hours/share chart and project milestones explain the work behind the site.
The 60 hours are an owner-reported estimate, not an independently measured time log. Category allocations are illustrative.
The methodology explains what the estimate includes and does not claim. No private conversations or tracking logs are published.

title: Contact forms with private admin delivery
summary: Send corrections, ideas, privacy requests and contributions inside the website, with confirmed private receipt and safer retries.
highlights: One responsive form shows only the fields needed for the selected topic. Name and reply email are optional.
Messages go to the restricted admin inbox, not to a public feed. No automatic notification email or automatic publication is sent.
A matching receipt appears only after storage confirmation. An unchanged retry uses the original request identifier to avoid another row.
Interrupted or uncertain delivery preserves the typed message and warns before edited text becomes a separate request. Privacy explains the active service.

title: Clearer quizzes, flashcards and mock exams
summary: Study practice now shares the Hub's visual identity with clearer questions, answer feedback and review summaries.
highlights: Course flashcards and question banks, lecture quizzes, statistics exercises, lab checks and mock exams use a consistent practice layout.
Lettered answer options, keyboard focus and responsive feedback make the interaction easier to follow.
Flashcard progress reflects the actual due-card session; starting a Health Economics mock opens the exam directly.
Existing content, scoring, identifiers, saved study progress and offline support are preserved.

links.label: Open study practice through your course

title: A clearer Support, Contact and Privacy experience
summary: Find the right support route more easily and read a reorganised privacy notice with compact source labels and accessible navigation.
highlights: Support includes a guided contact chooser, visible emergency guidance and expandable university support cards.
The three pages share navy, warm ivory and terracotta styling, phone-friendly navigation and keyboard-accessible controls.
Privacy describes local study data, offline copies, external requests and the difference between aggregate cohort counts and fictional directory profiles.
The complete prepared directory terms remain readable and printable. Registration and the editor backend remain inactive; the later Contact-form release is recorded separately.

title: New Academic Rules and Programme Journey layouts
summary: Browse academic guidance with a shared visual identity, easier section navigation and smaller complete source badges.
highlights: Academic Rules has a clearer re-sit guide, expandable university rules and a responsive grading comparison.
Programme Journey shows a track-aware four-semester route, stage details and organised degree, fee and grant guidance.
A desktop contents rail becomes a scrollable phone navigation bar; source labels use a compact 11px format without removing their names or dates.
Original qualifications, sources, saved-track behaviour, deep links and complete printing remain intact.

title: Seven new study, life and career workbenches
summary: Use practical local tools for economics, sample precision, study sessions, four-city budgets, moving, document dates and career applications.
highlights: Explore economics graphs and approximate sample precision, and organise personal study tasks with explicit capacity and unscheduled-hours feedback.
Build your own city-budget scenarios, moving checklists and document-deadline reminders; no city prices, exchange rates or official deadlines are invented.
The career tracker records opportunities, stages, next actions and follow-ups, alongside preparation checks.
Drafts stay in the tab unless explicitly saved on this device. Exports and reviewed imports are local; the tools do not submit applications or send background notifications.

title: Right to Health guides and an interactive casebook
summary: A source-led Right to Health workspace brings original study guides, case exercises, practice questions and revision aids together.
highlights: Ten original guides and source-located study sections help organise the course concepts and reading.
Explore progressive cases, multiple-choice practice, open-answer scaffolds, flashcards and glossary terms.
Existing course identifiers and study progress remain intact; case drafts stay page-local with text export.
Student-built explanations are distinct from authoritative sources. Official PDFs and recordings remain on their original platforms.

title: The Hub's own Pulse to Growth identity
summary: The selected Pulse to Growth mark unifies the unofficial Student Hub's header, app icons and sharing identity.
highlights: A rising pulse inside a rounded square is adapted to the navy, white and terracotta palette.
The shared header, navigation drawer, footer and app/browser assets use the selected mark.
This is the student project's own logo; it does not imply endorsement by the universities.

title: Redesigned guides for all four EU-HEM cities
summary: Explore Bologna, Oslo, Innsbruck and Rotterdam through illustrated covers, practical topic tabs and contextual information panels.
highlights: A new city directory and eight topic tabs make housing, arrival, transport, everyday life, study and safety information easier to find.
Search within each guide, save useful sections on your device, or use Read all for full reading and printing.
Original sources, review dates, cross-references and photo credits remain visible.
The layouts support phones, both themes, deep links and keyboard navigation.

title: Browse class days, exams and illustrated news from Home
summary: The homepage's everyday planning area lets you browse class days and upcoming exams, alongside an illustrated announcement carousel.
highlights: Step through days and exam entries without leaving the homepage, while retaining the saved-course filter.
Illustrated news cards link to the full announcement reader, with rotation and pause controls.
Motion respects reduced-motion preferences and the existing homepage navigation remains available.

title: Clearer release history and the November v2 plan
summary: Roadmap & Updates separates verified releases from Now, Next and Later work and shows the early-November v2 target alongside v1.
highlights: Published updates link to real successful deployments; future release windows remain explicitly labelled as targets.
The current public version stays Beta v0.9. v1.0 targets 15 October and v2.0 targets early November 2026.
Search, filters, saved plans and the journey timeline distinguish released features from planned work.
